text: Parent behaviour during interview: Parent 1 spontaneously praises child's qualities or behaviour at least twice during the visit. The key word here is 'spontaneous', but since most parents enjoy talking about and are proud of their children this is not hard to observe. Frequently a parent will tell you how well her child throws a ball or runs and will brag about how well he/she dresses himself/her
instrument: Parenting – Parental behaviour – Spontaneous praise during interview

text: Parent 1 scolds, shouts at, belittles or hits the child. The reprimand must be made directly to the child, e.g. not simply tell the interviewer that the child is bad. Hitting includes any physical reprimand (slapping, smacking etc) made in anger.
instrument: Parenting – Parental behaviour – Scolds, belittles shouts during interview

text: Child behaviour during interview: Degree of positive mood in response to you or Parent 1. Positive mood includes smiling, laughing, or sounded excited, happy or pleased. The ratings refer to both duration and intensity. NB Ignore the brief displays if there were intense or prolonged displays
instrument: Social and emotional outcomes – Temperament – Degree of positive response from Study Child to interviewer or P1

text: Degree of negative response in response to you or Parent 1. Negative mood includes fussing, pouting, whining, crying and vocal or physical expression of anger. The ratings refer to both duration and intensity. NB Ignore the brief displays if there were intense or prolonged displays
instrument: Social and emotional outcomes – Temperament – Degree of negative response from Study Child to interviewer or P1

text: Fear / trust. The extent to which child shows fear toward you when you make a social or physical approach toward the child or when you present material to the child. For example, a fearful child might try to hide behind his/her parent, bury his/her head in the parents lap, or be hesitant to even go into the room with you. A less fearful child may exhibit fear only when you get too close
instrument: Social and emotional outcomes – Temperament – Extent to which Study Child shows fear towards interviewer
